title: Atomic Pointers
goal: Use AtomicPtr to swap raw pointers atomically across threads.

sections.text: Beyond primitive numbers, Rust provides `AtomicPtr<T>` to manage raw pointers `*mut T` atomically.

sections.caption: AtomicPtr wraps a raw pointer *mut T.

sections.text: Reading or writing the `AtomicPtr` itself is safe Rust code. Dereferencing the raw pointer loaded from it requires an `unsafe` block.
`AtomicPtr` is the foundation for building lock-free data structures like lock-free stacks and queues.

sections.caption: Box::into_raw turns a Box into a raw pointer.

sections.text: Managing memory with `AtomicPtr` requires strict care. You must ensure heap allocations are reclaimed with `Box::from_raw` when discarded.

explanation: Use AtomicPtr to swap raw pointers atomically across threads.
